hook: A rocket dragged 350 feet of explosives across this desert.
narration: More than three hundred fifty feet of explosives, and all of it went off at once.
Marines of the 2nd Combat Engineer Battalion fired it at Twentynine Palms, California, on February first, 2021.
It is a MICLIC, a mine clearing charge. The line is packed with five pounds of C-4 for every foot.
A rocket drags the line out over a minefield. When it blows, buried mines go off or get shoved out of the way.
What is left behind is a cleared lane, eight meters wide and one hundred meters long.
They fired it from amphibious assault vehicles, and from a robot vehicle called the EMAV.
Then the next rocket arced over the desert, pulling its line behind it.
outcome: Seconds later that line went off in one long blast, and smoke swallowed the range.
title: 350 feet of C-4 goes off at once
description:
On Feb. 1, 2021, Marines with 2nd Combat Engineer Battalion, 2d Marine Division, fired M58 Mine Clearing Line Charges from Assault Amphibious Vehicles and from an Expeditionary Modular Autonomous Vehicle at Marine Corps Air-Ground Combat Center, Twentynine Palms, Calif.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Jessica Massi, 2nd Marine Division, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/782726/fire-whole
